{
  "schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "case_id": "pilot-010",
  "decision": "REMAIN_CLASSICAL",
  "candidate_regions": [
    {
      "file": "program.py",
      "function": "contains_record",
      "start_line": 4,
      "end_line": 8
    }
  ],
  "structural_eligibility": true,
  "practical_suitability": false,
  "benchmark_supported": null,
  "computational_intent": "Parse every supplied JSON string before searching, preserving malformed-JSON exceptions, and then return the exact Boolean existence result for a record whose active field is truthy and whose key equals the requested target under Python semantics.",
  "migration_family": "unstructured_search",
  "contract_applicability": [
    {
      "contract_id": "grover-predicate-v0",
      "applicable": true,
      "rationale": "After all payloads have been parsed, the finite record indices admit the Boolean predicate active(record[i]) and key(record[i]) == target. Applicability remains conditional on a reversible implementation of Python truthiness and equality, explicit fresh-batch data encoding, and exact handling of the no-match outcome."
    },
    {
      "contract_id": "qubo-ising-v0",
      "applicable": false,
      "rationale": "The program performs an existence test over independent records and supplies no optimization objective, interacting binary decisions, or constraints whose optimum must be found. Recasting existence as an artificial QUBO would not establish suitability and would introduce approximate-solution concerns absent from the original exact Boolean contract."
    }
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The finite candidate domain is the set of indices in the fully parsed records list.",
    "JSON parsing remains classical and completes for every payload before any search begins.",
    "Any quantum formulation must account for constructing a coherent representation of every fresh batch and of the target.",
    "Padded basis states outside the actual record count are treated as unmarked."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Fresh coherent data preparation has at least batch-wide work and may eliminate any query-complexity benefit over the linear classical scan.",
    "There is no supplied QRAM, reusable oracle, scale information, cost model, or benchmark evidence.",
    "Reversibly reproducing Python truthiness and equality for the allowed JSON values may require substantial encoding and workspace.",
    "Ordinary Grover-style search is probabilistic, whereas the software contract requires an exact Boolean result, especially for the no-match case.",
    "Classical verification can validate a returned match but cannot by itself certify absence; a complete classical fallback would preserve exactness while undermining practical benefit.",
    "The parsing cost and malformed-JSON behavior cannot be skipped or hidden by early quantum search."
  ],
  "rationale": "Lines 4-8 are structurally expressible as finite predicate search, so a conditional Grover-style formulation exists. Lines 11-13, however, require every fresh classical payload to be parsed before searching. With no coherent data oracle or reusable state, each invocation must incur parsing and batch-wide coherent encoding costs. The classical search is already linear, while exact no-match certification introduces either an unresolved error-policy change or a full classical fallback. No approved cost model or benchmark establishes an end-to-end benefit. The search loop is therefore a structurally plausible candidate but not a practically supported quantumization opportunity under the stated execution assumptions.",
  "plan": {
    "schema_version": "0.1.0",
    "contract_id": "grover-predicate-v0",
    "computational_intent_id": "exact_active_record_key_existence_after_full_json_parsing",
    "migration_family": "unstructured_search",
    "formulation": "Retain line 12 as a complete classical parsing phase. Over record indices i, define P(i) to be true exactly when i is in range, Python truthiness of records[i][\"active\"] is true, and records[i][\"key\"] equals target under the original Python comparison semantics. Mark only states satisfying P. A reversible implementation of those semantics and an unknown-number-of-matches search procedure are required. Exact absence remains unresolved unless a complete classical fallback is used.",
    "input_encoding": "For every fresh batch, encode an index register and construct coherent access to the parsed active and key values, with out-of-range padded indices marked false. Encode the target and all workspace needed for reversible truthiness and equality. Parsing, representation construction, uncomputation, and their linear-in-batch costs must be included; no free QRAM or prebuilt oracle is assumed.",
    "quantum_algorithm_family": "grover_style",
    "output_decoding": "Measure a candidate index and classically verify the corresponding parsed record using the original predicate. If no verified candidate is produced, preserving the exact classical result requires a complete classical scan before returning false. Replacing that scan with a probabilistic no-solution decision would weaken the software contract and requires an explicit, currently absent error policy. Parsing exceptions must propagate before this phase exactly as in the original program.",
    "assumptions": [
      "A reversible circuit can exactly implement the relevant Python truthiness and equality behavior for all permitted JSON field values.",
      "All payloads are parsed before oracle construction or search, preserving the specified exception behavior.",
      "The record count and encoded field sizes fit the chosen representation; no physical feasibility is claimed."
    ],
    "risks": [
      "Oracle and coherent-memory construction may cost as much as or more than the classical scan.",
      "Unknown marked-item count complicates amplitude-amplification scheduling.",
      "Noise and finite sampling do not provide deterministic no-solution certification.",
      "An exact classical fallback removes the principal opportunity for end-to-end acceleration.",
      "Resource counts, hardware feasibility, and advantage are unresolved."
    ],
    "expected_resource_characteristics": {
      "status": "unresolved unless justified"
    }
  }
}
